lessons.title: Reading and Interpreting Tables
lessons.concept: Data interpretation questions present information in tables, charts, or graphs. Start by reading titles, headings, units, and totals carefully. Identify exactly what the question asks for before performing calculations, and locate the correct row/column values.
lessons.formula: Steps: understand labels/units -> locate required data -> apply arithmetic (sum, difference, ratio, percentage) -> verify against options.
lessons.worked_example: If a table shows sales of A=120, B=80, C=100 units, total = 120+80+100 = 300. Share of B = (80/300)*100 = 26.67% (approx).
mistakes: Reading values from the wrong row or column
Calculating percentage of the wrong base/total

lessons.title: Percentages and Ratios from Data
lessons.concept: Many DI questions require converting table values into percentages, ratios, or comparisons. Percentage = (part/whole)*100. Ratio compares two quantities in simplest form. Always confirm the base (which total or which category) used for comparison.
lessons.formula: Percentage = (value / base) * 100. Ratio a:b = a/b simplified. Percentage change = ((new-old)/old)*100.
mistakes: Using the new value as denominator for percentage increase instead of the original value
Not simplifying ratios to lowest terms
Confusing percentage points with percentage change

lessons.title: Averages and Comparisons
lessons.concept: DI sets often ask for averages across categories/years or comparisons (highest/lowest/difference). Average = sum of values / number of values. For comparisons, compute or estimate carefully and avoid assumptions not supported by data.
lessons.formula: Average = (sum of observations) / (count of observations). Difference = |value1 - value2|.
lessons.worked_example: Values 40, 55, 65, 80 over 4 years: average = (40+55+65+80)/4 = 240/4 = 60. Highest-lowest difference = 80 - 40 = 40.
mistakes: Dividing by wrong count (including/excluding categories incorrectly)
Comparing values without aligning to the same unit/base
Rounding too early and selecting the wrong option
